subject: Post-demo follow-up: recommended models, pricing & regression concerns
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Claire Park <claire@finlytics.com>, Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: recommended models, pricing & regression concerns

Hi Claire / Alex —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the model slate we think is worth piloting based on the demo signals (latency targets, accuracy on numeric extraction, and cost sensitivity):

High-level ask from you: low-latency chat for analysts (target p95 < 400ms), reliable numeric extraction from filings, and predictable per-query cost for ~50k monthly active queries.

Recommended shortlist (initially 3 variants we can A/B in the pilot):
- Redwood-Instruct-7B-q4 (quantized): best cost profile for high throughput; expect 2–3x cost savings vs 8-bit large models. Good on short-context Q&A and numeric extraction when prompted with the structured prompt set. Estimated cost: ~$0.0025/response (median-length).
- Orca-Mini-13B-q8 (latency-optimized): slightly higher token cost but better at preserving accuracy on longer context windows; p95 latency ~300–380ms on our Dedicated pool with continuous batching. Estimated cost: ~$0.004/response.
- LlamaX-34B-8bit-hybrid: highest fidelity, lowest hallucination on complex financial reasoning; slower and more expensive — reserve for worst-case fallbacks or for small percentage of traffic where precision matters. Estimated cost: ~$0.012/response.

Attachments: I attached the benchmark CSV and the prompt pack we used during the demo. I also included the latency heatmap (p50/p95 across our rack).

Risks and immediate asks:
- Regression risk: numeric extraction F1 drops when prompts are not structured; recommend a 200-example eval set that mirrors your quarterly filings to validate patterns.
- Prompt-sensitivity: some models truncate long tables — we suggest a KV caching + prefix strategy for recurring report templates.
- Rollout plan: start with Redwood-Instruct on 60% traffic, Orca-Mini on 30%, LlamaX on 10% for critical queries. Monitor quality metrics (extraction F1, hallucination rate) and cost per session for 2 weeks before rebalancing.

Next steps I propose:
1) Share the 200-sample eval set (you) — helps us run targeted regression checks.
2) We run a 72-hour A/B run in our staging Dedicated pool and push results to the shared Drive link (we’ll include full token-level costing).
3) Quick sync after 72 hours to decide which model(s) to promote to production.

Timing: If you can share the eval set by Tue 9/22, we can get the A/B run started Wed 9/23.

Thanks —
Sooj
SoojIN Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Claire Park <claire@finlytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: recommended models, pricing & regression concerns

Thanks Sooj — this is helpful and aligned with what we heard internally. A few clarifying questions before we prepare the eval set:

1) For the Redwood-Instruct-7B-q4, what is the expected degradation on multi-step math/table extraction vs the LlamaX model? Even a small drop in F1 is costly for compliance workflows.
2) For the A/B run: can we force 0% traffic to LlamaX initially and run it as an isolated baseline? We want to understand headroom without inflating costs.
3) Any special prompting patterns you recommend for the ORCA/Orca-Mini model to reduce hallucinations on ticker lookups?

We’ll aim to share the 200-sample set by Tue; we may redact some PII first.

—Claire
Director, Data Products, Finlytics
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Claire Park <claire@finlytics.com>, Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: recommended models, pricing & regression concerns

Claire — great questions. Short answers + operational notes below.

1) Redwood-Instruct-7B-q4 vs LlamaX-34B: on our internal numeric extraction bench (the 1k-sample financial table set) we see ~3–5 point drop in extraction F1 on average for the quantized 7B vs the 34B. However, with targeted prompt templates (attached) and a small post-processing extractor (regex/parse fallback) we close most of that gap. If compliance requires near-100% recall on certain fields, reserve those to the LlamaX baseline.

2) Yes — we can run LlamaX as isolated baseline at 0% production traffic. For the A/B in staging we’ll run: Redwood-Instruct (A), Orca-Mini (B), and LlamaX isolated (C) — three separate lanes. We’ll provide per-lane metrics and cost breakdown.

3) For Orca-Mini prompt patterns:
- Prepend a one-line canonicalization step: "If the user asks for a ticker or numeric, always return canonical symbol and an ISO date-stamped value."
- Avoid embedding raw HTML tables; convert to pipe-delimited first (we include a converter in the prompt pack).
- Use the short system instruction to prefer "I don’t know" over guessing for unknown tickers.

Operational asks for your team: please include examples of the edge-case filings (tables with merged cells, footnote-linked numbers) in the 200-sample set — those stress the models differently.

I’ve started the staging job template and attached the small prompt pack with canonicalization examples. Ben / Marissa — can you run the 72-hour staging A/B once Claire confirms the sample set delivery date? Dylan — we’ll need the KV cache tweak enabled for the ORCA lane; estimate 2 hours of infra config.

—Sooj
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: recommended models, pricing & regression concerns

Claire —

We’ll plan to: 
- Kick off the three-lane staging run on Wed 9/23 once we get your eval set.
- LlamaX lane will be isolated (no production mimic) so you get clean baseline numbers.
- Deliverables after 72 hours: per-model latency heatmap, token-level costing CSV, extraction F1/confusion breakdown, and prompt-triggered hallucination samples.

We’ll also provide a quick playbook for reducing token cost using continuous batching and prefix caching if you decide to promote Redwood-Instruct.

If that timeline works, Claire — please send the eval set (redacted) to the Drive link and CC me. I’ll own the run and share the dashboard on the HubSpot deal.

Thanks —
Ben
